title.vi: Chiếc laptop thất lạc ở trường đại học

summary.en: A lecturer's laptop with the final exam files disappears from a seminar room. Was it stolen, or did something else happen?
summary.vi: Chiếc laptop chứa đề thi cuối kỳ của một giảng viên biến mất khỏi phòng học. Nó bị đánh cắp hay đã có chuyện gì khác xảy ra?

briefing.en: It is Thursday 14 October 2027. On Tuesday, Dr. Helen Park, a lecturer at Riverside University, lost her laptop after teaching in Room B204. The laptop contains the files for next week's final exam. Some students say the cleaner stole it, but nobody has any proof. Dr. Park has asked the English Detective Agency to find out what really happened. Read the notices, the schedule and the logs, interview the people involved and work out where the laptop is now. Then write an email to Dr. Park with your findings.
briefing.vi: Hôm nay là thứ Năm, ngày 14 tháng 10 năm 2027. Hôm thứ Ba, TS. Helen Park, giảng viên Trường Đại học Riverside, bị mất laptop sau buổi dạy ở phòng B204. Chiếc laptop chứa các tệp đề thi cuối kỳ của tuần sau. Một số sinh viên cho rằng cô lao công đã lấy trộm, nhưng không ai có bằng chứng. TS. Park đã nhờ English Detective Agency tìm ra sự thật. Hãy đọc các thông báo, lịch đặt phòng và nhật ký, phỏng vấn những người liên quan và xác định chiếc laptop hiện đang ở đâu. Sau đó viết email gửi TS. Park trình bày kết quả điều tra.

objectives.en: Read the notices and compare the times in the schedule and the logs.
objectives.vi: Đọc các thông báo và đối chiếu thời gian trong lịch đặt phòng và nhật ký.

objectives.vi: Viết email cho TS. Park giải thích chuyện đã xảy ra và cô nên làm gì.

documents.title: Missing laptop – Room B204
documents.body:
Dear colleagues and students,

My laptop has gone missing from Room B204. It is a silver Novatek AirBook 14. It has a small staff label on the bottom with the number RU-STAFF-0457.

This morning I taught Academic English 2 in Room B204 from 09:00 to 11:00. At 11:05 I left the room quickly because I had a faculty meeting in Room A101. I think I left my laptop on the front table next to the projector.

When I came back at 13:50, the room was empty and my laptop was not there. I went to the Security Office at 14:00. They had a silver laptop from Room B204, but it was not mine because it had a robotics club sticker on it.

The laptop contains the files for the final exam on Monday 25 October. I am sure nobody can open the files without my password.

If you have any information, please contact me or the Security Office (Room A005).

Thank you,
Dr. Helen Park
School of Languages

documents.title: Security Camera Summary – Corridor B2 and Security Office

meta.Cameras: B2-03 (corridor outside B204), A0-01 (Security Office desk)

documents.body:
Summary of camera recordings. To protect privacy, faces and names are not included in this summary.

Tuesday 12 October 2027 (camera B2-03):
- 11:06 – A woman with a staff card leaves B204 with a handbag and some papers. She is not carrying a laptop.
- 11:10 – About twenty students enter B204 for the 11:15 class.
- 13:03 – A male student with a red backpack leaves B204. He is carrying a silver laptop under his arm.
- 13:05 – The last students leave B204. No other person enters B204 between 13:05 and 13:20.
- 13:20 – A cleaner with a cleaning trolley enters B204.
- 13:31 – The cleaner leaves B204 with one silver laptop and walks towards the Security Office.

Wednesday 13 October 2027 (camera A0-01):
- 08:10 – The same male student with the red backpack hands in a silver laptop at the Security Office desk.
- 08:15 – He shows his student ID card and collects item LF-117.

Note: the doors of B204 were not damaged, and the alarm did not ring on either day.

questions.prompt: The notice says that LF-118 was found in Room B240. Why might LF-118 still be Dr. Park's laptop? Answer in 1–3 sentences.
keyPoints: There is no Room B240: rooms on the second floor of Building B are numbered B201 to B212.
B240 is probably a writing mistake for B204 (the same numbers in a different order).
LF-118 is the same model as Dr. Park's laptop (a silver Novatek AirBook 14) and was handed in the morning after it disappeared.
questions.sampleAnswer: Room B240 does not exist, because the rooms on the second floor are numbered B201 to B212, so it is probably a mistake for B204. Also, LF-118 is a silver Novatek AirBook 14, the same model as Dr. Park's laptop, and it was handed in the next morning.

facts.text: Dr. Park left Room B204 in a hurry at 11:05 for a faculty meeting, and she thinks she left her laptop on the front table.
Dr. Park's laptop has a staff label with the number RU-STAFF-0457 on the bottom, and it has no stickers on it.
Dr. Park read the lost-and-found notice on Wednesday, but she only looked for Room B204. She thought LF-117 was the student laptop with the robotics sticker.
The exam files are protected by a password, and Dr. Park also keeps a copy on the university cloud drive.

characters.name: Lucas Nguyen
characters.role: Second-year student in the Business Statistics class (Group S1)
characters.personality: Honest, shy and a bit embarrassed; gives short answers and apologises often.
characters.background: Lucas is a member of the university robotics club. He gave a group presentation in Room B204 on Tuesday from 11:15 to 13:00.
characters.greeting: Hi... I'm Lucas. I heard people are talking about a missing laptop. I'll try to help.

facts.text: Lucas put his laptop on the front table in Room B204 at about 11:20 for his group presentation. Another silver laptop was already on the table.
Lucas's own laptop is also a silver Novatek AirBook 14, and it has a robotics club sticker on the top.
At home on Tuesday evening, Lucas's password did not work on the laptop in his bag, and there was no robotics sticker on it. He realised he had taken the wrong laptop.
On Wednesday at 08:10, Lucas gave the laptop to the Security Office and collected his own laptop. He did not open any files and did not know whose laptop it was.

characters.role: Campus Security Officer, Security Office (Room A005)
characters.personality: Calm, careful and friendly; likes facts and clear times, and protects people's privacy.
characters.background: Omar has worked in Campus Security for five years. He looks after the lost-and-found items and checks the security cameras when something goes missing.

facts.text: Omar checked the camera recordings from the corridor outside Room B204 and from the Security Office desk, and he wrote a camera summary on Wednesday.
Item LF-118 is still in the Security Office safe. It has a staff label on the bottom with the number RU-STAFF-0457.
Omar wrote the handover form for LF-118 himself at a busy time on Wednesday morning, and he may have written the room number wrongly.
To collect a university laptop, a staff member must show a staff card and give the asset number of the laptop.

conclusion.question: What most probably happened to Dr. Park's laptop?

options.text: A student from the next class took it by mistake because his laptop is the same model. He handed it in to Security, and it is now item LF-118.
The cleaner stole the laptop when she cleaned Room B204.
An unknown person entered Room B204 after the class and stole the laptop.
Someone took the laptop and sold it on Campus Market.

unsupportedClaims: The cleaner stole the laptop (the log and the cameras show she handed in the laptop she found).
The laptop was sold on Campus Market (the post was from the night before it went missing).
The student wanted to steal the exam files (he returned the laptop the next morning and did not know whose it was).
Someone broke into Room B204 (the doors were not damaged and nobody entered between 13:05 and 13:20).

writingTask.prompt: Write an email to Dr. Helen Park. Tell her what most probably happened to her laptop, describe the evidence you found, explain where the laptop is now and tell her what she should do next. Use a polite and clear email style.
writingTask.audience: Dr. Helen Park, School of Languages, Riverside University
keyPoints: Explains that the laptop was not stolen but taken by mistake by a student from the next class with the same model.
Uses the camera summary: the student left B204 with a silver laptop at 13:03 and handed in a laptop on Wednesday at 08:10.
Identifies the laptop as item LF-118 and explains that 'Room B240' is a mistake, because rooms are numbered B201 to B212.
Shows that the claim about the cleaner is not supported (she handed in LF-117).
Tells Dr. Park to collect the laptop at Room A005 with her staff card and asset number RU-STAFF-0457.

documents: Start with Dr. Park's email and the room booking schedule.
Compare the times in the schedule, the cleaning log and the lost-and-found notice.
Look carefully at the room numbers on the lost-and-found notice. Do all these rooms really exist?
evidence: Highlight times, room numbers and descriptions of laptops.
Some messages in the group chat are only guesses or rumours, and one message is about something else.
Match each laptop on the lost-and-found list with the person who handed it in.
interviews: Ask the Security Office whether anyone has checked the cameras.
Ask Lucas about his presentation and about his own laptop.
Ask Dr. Park how she read the lost-and-found notice.
analysis: Verified evidence comes from logs, schedules, notices and camera records; guesses in the chat are unverified.
Follow the laptop: who carried it out of the room, and where did it go next?
Check whether any evidence really shows that someone wanted to steal it.
report: Organise your email: greeting and purpose, what happened, evidence, where the laptop is now, next steps.
Use polite phrases such as 'I am writing to…', 'I would suggest…' and 'Kind regards'.
Tell Dr. Park exactly where to go and what to bring.

sampleSolution.report:
Dear Dr. Park,

I am writing to tell you the results of my investigation into your missing laptop. The good news is that it was not stolen.

On 12 October, the Business Statistics class used Room B204 after your class. One student in that class has the same silver Novatek AirBook 14. During the presentations both laptops were on the front table, and the cameras show him leaving the room with a silver laptop at 13:03. He took yours by mistake.

The cleaner found his laptop and handed it in to Security as LF-117, so the claim that she stole your laptop is not true. On Wednesday at 08:10, the same student handed in your laptop and collected his own. On the lost-and-found notice it is item LF-118, but the room is written as B240. There is no Room B240 on the second floor, so this is probably a writing mistake.

Please go to the Security Office in Room A005 with your staff card and the asset number RU-STAFF-0457 to collect it.

Kind regards,
Student Detective
